content.title: About
content.content: Kale (Brassica oleracea var. acephala) is a leafy cruciferous vegetable renowned for its high nutrient density. The frozen, cooked, fat‑added product is a ready‑to‑eat side dish that retains most of the vitamins and minerals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Kale is often called a “superfood” because of its rich micronutrient profile.
It contains more vitamin K than spinach by several folds.
Freezing preserves up to 90 % of its antioxidants, which can degrade in fresh kale during long storage.
Traditionally, Scandinavians cooked kale with lard or butter to improve flavor and texture.
Kale can be used as a rice substitute in low‑carb diets.

items.title: Rich in vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: High antioxidant content
items.content: Kale provides vitamin C, beta‑carotene and flavonoids that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Its fiber promotes regular bowel movements and a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Source of minerals
items.content: Kale supplies calcium, magnesium and iron, important for bones, muscles and blood formation.

items.title: Cardiovascular support
items.content: Potassium and low sodium levels help maintain healthy blood pressure.

items.title: Thyroid considerations
items.content: Kale contains glucosinolates, which in large amounts may affect thyroid function.

items.title: Cruciferous allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to Brassicaceae vegetables.

items.title: Added fat content
items.content: Because the product already includes fat, people monitoring calories should account for it in their daily intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the frozen portion in a skillet or microwave, stirring to distribute the added fat evenly. Serve as a side dish with meat, fish, or mixed into vegetable medleys. Enhance flavor with herbs, garlic or a squeeze of lemon.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the product frozen at –18 °C (0 °F) or lower. Once thawed, consume within 2–3 days and store in an airtight container in the refrigerator.
